title: Felix and the Lantern
premise: In the river city of Vellamont, on the eve of revolution, Quentin Ashgrove works as a compositor in their late father's print shop, hiding their identity behind the name of a dead brother, Felix. When a census taker named Ilse notices that the shop's ledgers record two children but only one ever appears, Quentin realizes the state has begun assembling lists of people like them—people who exist in ink but not in law. The evidence of who is being marked for removal lies in a misprinted census plate still locked in the shop's press room, and Quentin must carry it past three checkpoints to the underground printers before the purge orders are typeset. Along the way they gather an unlikely family—a smuggler, a defrocked priest, and Ilse herself, who must choose between her oath and her conscience—and learn that inheritance is not what your father left you, but what you refuse to surrender. In the end, the plate reaches the underground press, the truth is printed and scattered through the city, and Quentin claims both names—Felix and Ashgrove—as their own.
about_author: Elodie Pemberton is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in coastal mill towns. Their fiction explores the lives of people history recorded only in margins and misprints.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A day in the Ashgrove print shop: setting type by lamplight, measuring everything by what can be carried in one satchel. Establishes the hidden second bed, the brother's name worn like a coat. Emotional beat: quiet vigilance mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: The Census Taker's Question
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Ilse arrives with the household census; her pen pauses over 'number of children.' Quentin answers 'one,' and watches her write something else. Emotional beat: the first crack in invisibility, dread blooming under courtesy.

chapters.title: What Father Left
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with flashback. Sorting the father's effects after his death, Quentin finds his will naming 'my child' without a name—the only document in the city that affirms them. Emotional beat: grief braided with fragile hope.

chapters.title: Felix Answers the Door
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She returns with follow-up questions; 'Felix' receives her at the door, voice pitched wrong. She notices the hands—compositor's hands, ink-stained, familiar from the first visit. Emotional beat: suspicion softening into curiosity she doesn't yet trust.

chapters.title: The Misprint
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Cleaning the press room, Quentin discovers a rejected census plate: the master list of households flagged for 'correction,' including their own address. Emotional beat: terror crystallizing into purpose—the plate is proof, and proof can be printed.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Scouting the route to the underground printers: the bridge guard, the customs house, the cathedral gate. Each checkpoint demands papers Quentin cannot safely show. Emotional beat: the map of the city becomes a map of their own vulnerability.

chapters.title: A Smuggler's Rate
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. The canal smuggler Dario agrees—for a price—to move cargo he hasn't seen. He clocks Quentin's fear and recognizes it as the real currency. Emotional beat: transactional loyalty, offered with a wink and held loosely.

chapters.title: The Defrocked Priest
chapters.summary: Father Anselm's POV. At the cathedral gate, the disgraced priest who lost his post for sheltering the unregistered offers Quentin sanctuary and a warning: the purge orders go to press within the fortnight. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption through someone else's danger.

chapters.title: Ilse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. At home, Ilse reviews her own census rolls and finds her supervisor altering entries—households vanishing before her eyes. She copies a page in secret. Emotional beat: the moment duty curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin hides the plate inside a forme of wedding invitations and runs the route once, unarmed and empty-handed, learning the guards' rhythms. Emotional beat: fear disciplined into craft, the printer's patience applied to survival.

chapters.title: The Raid Next Door
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interwoven. Soldiers empty the tailor's shop across the lane; the family is gone by morning. Quentin watches from the type gallery, plate hidden beneath the floor. Emotional beat: horror as instruction—this is what failure looks like.

chapters.title: What Dario Carries
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Dario learns what's in the crate when soldiers nearly open it at the customs house; he lies for the first time in his career and doesn't know why. Emotional beat: a mercenary discovering he has acquired stakes.

chapters.title: Anselm's Bargain
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Anselm offers to sanctify the plan—his gate is the third checkpoint—but demands the plate be printed openly, with his name on it. Emotional beat: pride wrestling with penance; he wants to be seen paying.

chapters.title: Ilse Comes Back
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse returns to the shop after hours and tells Quentin the truth: their household is flagged, the orders are being typeset, and she has copied pages proving the lists were falsified. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted—an agent of the state defecting toward the people she counted.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Quentin's POV. In the print shop after midnight: Quentin, Dario, Anselm, and Ilse plan together over bread and lamp oil, strangers becoming something like kin. Emotional beat: warmth as defiance—they have built the family the ledger denied.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Quentin and Dario's POV, alternating. The bridge crossing goes wrong when a guard recognizes Dario's boat; they bluff through with forged wedding invitations as cover. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the knowledge that the forgery is now evidence against them all.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Customs House
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Her supervisor, suspicious of her queries, follows her and finds the copied pages. She is arrested—but not before sending a warning note to the shop. Emotional beat: sacrifice without certainty; loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. With Ilse taken, the customs house pass is void. Quentin must walk through as themselves—no alias, no Felix—using their father's will as identification. Emotional beat: claiming their true name at the moment of greatest danger.

chapters.title: The Cathedral Gate
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Anselm holds the gate while soldiers arrive demanding the fugitive compositor; he bars the door with his body and his office. Quentin slips through the crypt passage carrying the plate. Emotional beat: courage passed hand to hand like a relay baton.

chapters.title: Press Night
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the underground print shop, Quentin sets the plate and pulls the first proofs of the true census—the names of everyone marked for removal. Emotional beat: the compositor's art turned into testimony; grief and exaltation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ashes and Ink
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax resolution. Soldiers burn the Ashgrove shop; the printed sheets are already loose in the city, passed hand to hand. Ilse escapes custody because the guards themselves have read the lists and found their own families on them. Emotional beat: loss transfigured—the building dies so the truth survives.

chapters.title: Felix and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Quentin's POV. Months later, in the free city, Quentin hangs a lantern over a new print shop's door and sets their father's will in a frame beside the press. They sign the first broadside 'Q. Ashgrove, called Felix.' Emotional beat: inheritance claimed—found family gathered beneath the light, printing tomorrow.
